promptLatex: Two tangents drawn from an external point $P$ touch a circle with centre $O$ at $A$ and $B$, and the minor arc $AB$ measures $140^{\circ}$. What is the measure of $\angle APB$, in degrees?
hintLatex: Use the right angles that sit at the two points of tangency.
The four angles of quadrilateral $AOBP$ add up to a full turn, and two of them are right angles.
solutionLatex:
At the point of tangency the radius is perpendicular to the tangent, so $\angle OAP = 90^{\circ}$ and $\angle OBP = 90^{\circ}$.

The angles of quadrilateral $AOBP$ therefore satisfy $m\angle AOB + m\angle APB + 90^{\circ} + 90^{\circ} = 360^{\circ}$.

The central angle $m\angle AOB$ stands on the minor arc $AB$, so it measures $140^{\circ}$. That gives $m\angle APB = 360^{\circ} - 90^{\circ} - 90^{\circ} - 140^{\circ} = 40^{\circ}$, which is the general rule $180^{\circ}$ minus the minor arc.
